description.text: Bentley Systems is the infrastructure engineering software company. Our purpose is to advance the world’s infrastructure for better quality of life. Our mission is to reshape how infrastructure systems and critical resources are delivered and optimized. We were founded in 1984 by the Bentley brothers and on September 25, 2020, we completed our initial public offering (“IPO”). Our enduring commitment is to develop and support the most comprehensive portfolio of integrated software offerings across disciplines, sectors, geographies, and the infrastructure lifecycle, enabling digital workflows that improve project delivery and asset performance.

about.description_short: Around the world, infrastructure professionals rely on software from Bentley Systems to help them design, build, and operate better and more resilient infrastructure for transportation, water, energy, cities, and more. Founded in 1984 by engineers for engineers, Bentley is the partner of choice for engineering firms and owner-operators worldwide, with software that spans engineering disciplines, industry sectors, and all phases of the infrastructure lifecycle. Through our digital twin solutions, we help infrastructure professionals unlock the value of their data to transform project delivery and asset performance.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 5,800 full-time colleagues globally, including approximately 2,400 in the Americas (the U.S., Canada, and Latin America, including the Caribbean); approximately 1,600 in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (“EMEA”); and approximately 1,800 in Asia-Pacific (“APAC”).

analysis_md:
# BSY — Bentley Systems, Incorporated
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-19. Market cap $11.781B at $35.37 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The infrastructure engineering software company: MicroStation and the Open applications (OpenRoads, OpenRail, OpenBuildings), ProjectWise collaboration, the iTwin digital-twin platform, plus acquired platforms Seequent (geosciences, ~$1.05B in 2021) and Power Line Systems (~$700M in 2022) and Cesium (geospatial). Subscriptions are 92% of revenue; ARR was $1,536M at Q2 2026, up 12% in constant currency, with a 109% dollar-based net revenue retention rate and 99% account retention (Q2 2026 results release). End markets are public works/utilities, resources (mining was the fastest-growing sector in Q2 2026) and industrial facilities — a largely counter-cyclical base.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $538,464,000; capex $18,255,000; SBC $72,576,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $447.6M = $1.34/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $447.6M, latest FY OE/share $1.34)
- Maintenance version: not printed for FY2023–25 — the annual D&A tag is blank in those years in financials_history.csv (statements.json carries D&A only as a quarterly series, ~$16M per quarter), so no maintenance figure is quoted rather than a hand-built one.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $1.126B (key_numbers.md).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $538,464,000 − prior YTD $280,500,000 + current YTD $264,921,000 = **TTM $522,885,000**
- Capex: FY $18,255,000 − prior YTD $7,135,000 + current YTD $13,266,000 = **TTM $24,386,000**
- SBC: FY $72,576,000 − prior YTD $36,995,000 + current YTD $42,940,000 = **TTM $78,521,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **320,435,795** — below the FY2025 diluted count of 333,089,213, after the January 2026 retirement of the $678M 2026 convertible notes (which cut the fully diluted count by over 10M shares) and ongoing buybacks
- **TTM OE total $419,978,000 → base OE/share $1.31** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $1.04/share — not used as the base: it averages in FY2023 ($0.96/share) and FY2024 ($1.04/share), while the TTM figure ($1.31) sits just below the latest FY print ($1.34), so the TTM base is both more current and not the aggressive choice.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate-strong, not wide
Justification: sticky, mission-critical infrastructure engineering software with 99% account retention, 109% NRR and 81–82% gross margins, but ROIC has only recently reached 12.4% after years at 5–10% on an acquisition-heavy capital base, and larger rivals contest every adjacent workflow — a moderate-strong moat, not a wide one.
- FOR: Comprehensive infrastructure-only portfolio (MicroStation, OpenRoads/OpenRail, ProjectWise, iTwin, Seequent, Power Line Systems) embedded in engineering workflows across design, construction and operations; 99% account retention and 109% dollar-based net revenue retention (Q2 2026 release) — switching costs are real: project files, standards and DOT/utility workflows are built on Bentley formats; subscriptions are 92% of revenue and ARR was $1,536M at Q2 2026, growing 12% in constant currency — recurring, counter-cyclical public-works/utilities base; gross margin 81.5% in FY2025 and 81.8% TTM (fundamentals.json), up from 77.6% in FY2021 — pricing power with operating leverage (operating margin 17.5% FY2018 to 24.1% FY2025).
- AGAINST: ROIC only 7.8–12.4% over FY2023–25 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy series: 7.8% / 10.2% / 12.4%, after 4.9% in FY2021 and 8.2% in FY2022) — rising, but not wide-moat proof through a cycle; invested capital is swollen by acquisition goodwill (Seequent, Power Line Systems). Larger platform rivals — Autodesk, Hexagon, Trimble — compete across design/construction software with broader ecosystems. Growth is steady, not accelerating: revenue +11.0% FY2025, ARR guided +10.5–12.5% for FY2026; AI monetization is explicitly a later phase (adoption/validation first, per the Q2 2026 call). Programmatic M&A is part of the model — integration and goodwill risk recur, and leverage follows deals (net debt $1.126B).
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended growth is 12.05% (rev CAGR 5y 13.38%, 3y 10.96%, latest rev YoY 10.99%, OE/share CAGR 2y 18.39%). Against actual prints — FY2025 revenue +10.99%, Q2 2026 revenue +12.8% YoY, ARR +12% constant currency, and FY2026 guidance of revenue +11–13% in constant currency with ARR growth +10.5–12.5% — the 12.05% base start sits inside guidance and at the latest prints; no recalibration needed. Bull (16.1%) and super-bull (20.1%) starts are above every recent print: they are tail cases requiring AI monetization (management's stated "later" phase) plus acquisition contribution, which is why the bull/super-bull offsets were narrowed from the +5/+12pp defaults to +4/+8pp and carry only 25%/10% probability. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $35.37.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | 0.1% | 0.75 | Infrastructure budgets stall; growth goes flat, OE margin compresses | $7.23 | 4.97% |
| Bear | 25% | 7.0% | 0.90 | Growth halves from current prints; no AI uplift | $11.84 | 6.88% |
| Base | 30% | 12.0% | 1.00 | Guided trajectory decays normally over the CAP | $16.43 | 8.70% |
| Bull | 25% | 16.1% | 1.10 | AI Plus applications monetize; E365 expansion lifts NRR | $21.58 | 10.60% |
| Super bull | 10% | 20.1% | 1.25 | Sustained acceleration — AI at machine speed plus deal contribution | $29.24 | 13.15% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $16.93 (−52.1% vs price), IV@12% $23.01, IV@10% $29.85, weighted IRR 8.92%, base-case IRR 8.70%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 3.71%, terminal value 21.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.05x, net debt 2.58x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Even the super-bull case (13.15% IRR, IV@15% $29.24) sits below the $35.37 price — no scenario in the set clears the 15% hurdle at this price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, quoted above.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs OCF differ by >40% in 2024, 2025): structural, not a one-off. OCF runs far above net income because the big non-cash charges are added back in OCF: SBC of $74,417,000 in FY2024 and $72,576,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv — a real cost here, deducted in full in the OE base) and D&A running ~$16M per quarter in statements.json's quarterly series, plus a growing subscription deferred-revenue balance ($245,729,000 at FY2024 to $278,244,000 at FY2025, fundamentals.json). Net income is also tax-noisy (FY2023 carried a $143,241,000 tax benefit in financials_history.csv). The OE base is OCF-based throughout, so the divergence does not contaminate it; if anything, net income understates this company's cash generation.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.05x): real, and confidence is capped at medium because of it — but it does not change the verdict: the entire scenario range (4.97%–13.15% IRR) sits below the 15% hurdle.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D at 6.88% vs bull C at 10.60%): sized to the bear end — the final tier is D, the bear tier, and even the bull tier is only C.
- The preliminary run's HIGH_NET_DEBT flag does not appear in the final run: net debt / normalized OE is 2.58x in the final diagnostics. Leverage is still noted: net debt $1.126B, the $678M 2026 converts were repaid at maturity in January 2026 (funded by cash and a revolver draw), and $575M of 0.375% converts due mid-2027 remain outstanding.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *range* across defensible methods: the preliminary run (median base $1.04/share, default scenario offsets, moat 5) gave weighted IRR 7.67% and IV@15% $13.52; the final run (TTM base $1.31/share, moat 6, narrowed bull offsets) gives 8.92% and $16.93. Both are Tier D, by a wide margin — the method range here (D to D) is unusually tight for this sweep because the gap to the hurdle is large under every input set.
- Quality is not the debate: 92% subscription revenue, 109% NRR, 81.8% TTM gross margin, OE positive 5/5 years, TTM free cash flow $498,499,000 (fundamentals.json) and FY2026 FCF guided at $500–570M. The debate is purely price: at $35.37 the market is paying for growth and durability the OE stream does not yet deliver at a 15% discount rate.
- Risks: a growth deceleration below the guided 10.5–12.5% ARR band (the bear cases), Autodesk/Hexagon platform pressure, AI workflow disruption cutting both ways, acquisition-led goodwill build, and the mid-2027 convertible maturity against $1.126B of net debt.
- Margin of safety: none at this price on these numbers — the price is 52.1% above the weighted IV@15%. The stock clears a 15% hurdle only at or below $16.93, a 20% hurdle at $11.56 and a 25% hurdle at $8.67 (key_numbers.md hurdle prices).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.92% on the final inputs; method range D–D)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the OE base — filing-direct TTM with every leg filled; the scenario spread caps it at medium)
- One-liner: High-quality sticky infrastructure software, moat 6/10 — but at $35.37 the weighted IRR is only 8.9% (IV@15% $16.93); it does not clear 15% until roughly $16.93, so Tier D despite the franchise quality.
